description: A bulk image resizer for a whole folder at once, in your browser. Can you run shell commands? Then do not send base64: upload the file from disk with curl -F file=@<path> https://helpyself.com/api/v1/tools/bulk-image-resizer (same tool, same answer, much faster). A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

data.description: The image file's bytes, base64-encoded. Send the whole file as it is, up to 50 MB: do not crop, shrink or split it first. If you can run shell commands, do not write the base64 out yourself: send the file from disk with curl -F file=@<path> -F <option>=<value> https://helpyself.com/api/v1/tools/bulk-image-resizer (add -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" if you have one); the answer is the same JSON.

format.description: The output format. keep (the default) re-encodes in the same type as the input; the others convert. JPEG has no transparency, so transparent areas are flattened onto white.

maxEdge.description: The longest side of the result in pixels. The image is scaled down to fit inside this on its longer edge, keeping its aspect ratio. Never enlarges: an image already within the bound is returned as it is, with unchanged: true.

name.description: The original filename. Echoed back unchanged as the result's name.

quality.description: Encoder quality for JPEG and WebP, 0.1 (smallest) to 1 (largest). Has no effect on PNG, which is lossless.

type.description: The MIME type of the bytes in data: JPEG, PNG or WebP. Also the output type when format is keep.

name: bulk_image_resizer
title: Bulk Image Resizer
